record.original_question: Can the Bikbaev-Tarasov Backlund-transform method be adapted to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation i u_t = u_{xx} - 2 |u|^2 u on the half-line with Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, despite the singularities introduced when the solution is extended from x > 0 to x < 0?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open problem to use the Bikbaev-Tarasov method to solve the IBVP for defocusing NLS, iut = uxx - 2|u|2 u, with Robin boundary conditions at x = 0. In this case the Backlund transformation extending the solution from x > 0 to x < 0 introduces certain singularities which must be controlled and the long-time behavior of the solution of the IBVP will be very different from the case of focusing NLS.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the half-line,
   i u_t(x,t) = u_{xx}(x,t) - 2 |u(x,t)|^2 u(x,t),  for x > 0, t > 0,
with initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x) (sufficiently smooth and decaying) and homogeneous Robin boundary condition
   u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0,  for t > 0,
where q ∈ ℝ is a fixed coupling constant.

The Bikbaev–Tarasov method, originally developed for the focusing NLS equation, prescribes an explicit Bäcklund transformation that extends a solution defined for x > 0 (subject to a Robin boundary condition at x = 0) to a solution of the same equation on the whole line x ∈ ℝ; the extension is then analyzed by inverse scattering / Riemann–Hilbert techniques applied on the line, and one recovers the half-line solution by restriction. In the focusing case, this extension is regular.

In the defocusing case, the analogous Bäcklund transformation that produces an extension to x < 0 generically introduces singularities of the extended field, and the long-time behavior is expected to differ qualitatively from the focusing case (no decaying solitons on the line, but stationary half-line solitons compatible with the Robin condition).

Question. Can the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transform method be adapted, with control of the singularities introduced when the half-line solution is extended to x < 0, so as to give a complete inverse-scattering / Riemann–Hilbert solution of the initial-boundary value problem above for the defocusing NLS equation with Robin boundary conditions, including a rigorous derivation of the long-time asymptotics of u(x,t)?
artifact.category_tag: Integrable IBVPs / inverse scattering on the half-line
artifact.status_search_result: The defocusing NLS half-line IBVP with homogeneous Robin boundary conditions has been treated rigorously (Riemann–Hilbert representation, well-posedness in H^{1,1}, t^{-3/4} decay, asymptotic stability of stationary solitons) by Lee et al. (Proc. LMS, 2023), but those authors explicitly state that they adopted a different approach (unified transform method) because the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund extension introduces singularities that are difficult to control in the defocusing case. Thus the IBVP itself is solved by other means, while the specific question of adapting the Bikbaev–Tarasov method appears not to have been carried out and remains open.

status_evidence.title: The nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line with homogeneous Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: It is not trivial to generalize the approach of [Bikbaev–Tarasov] to the defocusing case, because when λ=1 the Bäcklund transformation extending the solution from x>0 to x<0 introduces certain singularities which must be controlled. This is one reason why we have decided to adopt a different approach.
status_evidence.claim: The defocusing IBVP with Robin BC has been solved via the unified transform method, while the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-extension approach was avoided due to singularities.

status_evidence.title: Lee, Lenells, Stenmark — NLS on the half-line with homogeneous Robin BC
status_evidence.snippet: Riemann–Hilbert representation, global well-posedness in H^{1,1}, long-time asymptotics including t^{-3/4} decay in the defocusing case and asymptotic stability of stationary solitons.
status_evidence.claim: The half-line defocusing NLS Robin IBVP is rigorously solved, but by a different method than Bikbaev–Tarasov.
